open_obligations: Check calibration specifically above 90% confidence, Michael et al.'s problem regime.
Note that Khan et al.'s questions may not include stalemate-inducing complex arguments.
Check whether the 75% threshold was chosen post hoc.
in.other_title: Confident human debate judgements are reliable: 94% accuracy keeping 65% of questions
in.rationale: Michael et al. hope eliciting judge uncertainty lets debate fail gracefully but find calibration hard at high confidence. Khan et al. report that rejecting judgements below 75% confidence retains 65% of questions at 94% accuracy and that judges are better calibrated with debate than consultancy; this does not test the case of arguments too complex for the judge.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether judge confidence can make debate fail gracefully, for human judges of LLM debates on QuALITY HARD

open_obligations: Check the calibration curve above 80% confidence under debate alone.
Note judges hold strong priors, unlike Michael et al.'s near-50/50 judges.
Check that Brier differences are not driven by accuracy differences alone.
in.other_title: Human judges are overconfident under both protocols; debate Brier 0.231 vs 0.335
in.rationale: Michael et al. find calibration difficult in the high-confidence regime. Rahman et al. report judges are overconfident under both debate and consultancy, most above 80% confidence, while debate improves Brier score (0.231 vs 0.335); this supports the difficulty and shows debate only partly helps.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether human judges of AI debate are well calibrated at high confidence, on COVID-19 claims

text: The authors state they have not shown debate extracts all of the debaters' knowledge: on some questions the best strategies of both debaters may produce arguments too complex for the judge, leading to a stalemate. They hope eliciting judge uncertainty lets debate fail gracefully, but this requires well-calibrated judges, which they find remains difficult in the high-confidence regime.
title: Debate may not extract all knowledge; too-complex arguments could stalemate the judge
